review_kind: visual inspection of every supplied native PNG plus receipt reconciliation
method: Opened and visually inspected all 16 PNGs individually with the local image viewer; did not infer visual results from receipt metadata. Parsed the receipt and independently recomputed each PNG SHA-256. No engine, source changes, image edits, or input automation were performed by this reviewer.
viewing_limits: The seven 1280x720 or smaller UI/map images and three 1280x720 direction sheets were inspected as delivered by the image viewer, as were both 1280x720 portraits and the 1280x720 timeline.

The tool reported downsampling the three 2560x1440 integer-zoom sheets to 2048x1152 for the model display. Their corresponding native 1280x720 sheets were also inspected. This is not a pixel-for-pixel 2560x1440 display-quality claim.
PASS means the stated static visual scope has no blocking defect observed; it is not overall gameplay, package, accessibility, or human acceptance.
LIMITED means the image exposes a specific readability or artwork limitation, or cannot establish continuous animation despite showing coherent static poses.

FAIL would mean a clear blocking defect within the stated static scope, such as absent champions, unreadable essential roster names, broken portrait identity, severe clipping, or a high-confidence heading inversion. None was found in these samples.
cross_image_findings: All 30 Gallery cards are visible at both captured sizes, in the intended Small/Middle/Large then name order. Long champion names wrap inside their cards rather than crossing card boundaries. Race columns and page controls are absent.

The 960x540 Gallery preserves the complete roster and details panel, but scaled helper, size, status and control text is small and less comfortable to read. This is not universal minimum-resolution readability acceptance.

The two refined portrait screens retain Joh's olive Orc identity and Grimm's violet Troll identity, including hair, tusks, ears, armor and Grimm's two side horns. Read-only inspection is visibly separate from the equipped Oh Tipi HUD identity and unavailable attunement state.

Farflow's service label is visibly low contrast at both map sizes. At 960x540, peripheral world labels and parts of the scene can fall beneath fixed HUD/quick-action panels; those captures do not establish complete service-discovery clarity.

Across all six direction sheets, front/back/profile progression is coherent with the disclosed distinction between travel A and aim B. Jump and walk face B; slide, roll and air dodge face A. No high-confidence cardinal-heading inversion or champion-identity substitution was observed.

Slide and roll visibly reuse the same low pose; air dodge reuses the airborne key. Stable held silhouettes remove obvious mesh distortion in these samples but do not supply authored slide, roll, strafe, backpedal or airborne-casting cycles.

The paid timeline visibly switches from aim-facing sprint to travel-facing slide, then back to aim-facing gather/jump. This matches the disclosed pose policy, but its perceived rotation abruptness needs continuous-motion human review.

The receipt reports ordinary paid simulation commands and separate controlled presenter fixtures. Static images cannot independently prove physical input, control latency, continuous-motion quality, route traversal, multiplayer behavior, or measured performance.

observations: Three size-profile rows and all six sample columns fit without sprite or annotation overlap. The displayed gather samples retain positive horizontal speed while speed decreases, followed by clearly lifted jump samples.
